title: The Broken Tally
subject: Python
intro: Sigrun's shield-order program crashes before it prints a single number. Read the error, repair the code and get the workshop's totals right.

objectives.label: Read a Python error message to find the problem
Fix a type error by converting a number to text
Write expressions that calculate from variables
Predict what a line of Python prints

badge.name: Code Mender
badge.description: Read a real error message and repaired a Python program.

takeaway: Error messages are clues, not insults: the last line names the problem. Calculate from variables instead of typing answers in, and convert numbers with str() before joining them to text.

scenes.title: The workshop
scenes.speaker: sigrun
lines: Ah, a Pathfinder! Mind the sawdust.
I wrote a little Python program to count this week's shield orders. Every time I run it, it shouts at me and stops.
Can you make sense of it? I'm better with timber than with text.

scenes.title: Read the error
scenes.speaker: sigrun
scenes.context: Here's the program and the message it shows.
scenes.code:
orders = [12, 7, 9, 4]
total = sum(orders)
print("Total shields: " + total)

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tally.py", line 3
TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
scenes.prompt: What is the error telling you?

options.text: Line 3 tries to join text and a number with +, and Python won't do that automatically
options.feedback: Exactly. "Total shields: " is text (str); total is a whole number (int). + can join text to text, not text to a number.

options.text: sum() can't add up a list
options.feedback: sum() worked fine on line 2. The error points at line 3.

options.text: The variable orders is spelled wrong
options.feedback: A misspelling gives a NameError. This is a TypeError, about mixing kinds of value.
The list is fine. The problem is what happens when the total is printed.

hints: Start with the last line of the error. It names the kind of problem and gives details.
"str" means text and "int" means a whole number. Which line mixes them?
scenes.explanation: Python errors end with the type of error and a description. TypeError means two kinds of value were combined in a way Python doesn't allow, here text (str) and a whole number (int).

scenes.title: Repair the print
scenes.speaker: sigrun
scenes.context: Now fix line 3 so it prints the total.
scenes.prompt: Replace the blank with an expression so the program prints: Total shields: 32
hints: Turn the number into text before joining it.
scenes.explanation: str() converts a value to text, so it can be joined to other text with +. Using the variable, not typing 32, means the program stays correct when orders change.

scenes.title: The weekly average
scenes.speaker: sigrun
scenes.context: Next, I need the average number of shields ordered per week.
scenes.prompt: Write an expression for the average of orders. The program prints the result.
scenes.successFeedback: The program prints 8.0: 32 shields over 4 weeks.
hints: An average is the total divided by how many values there are.
sum(orders) gives the total and len(orders) gives how many values there are.
scenes.explanation: sum(orders) / len(orders) works for any list. Note that / always gives a decimal in Python, so the program prints 8.0 rather than 8.

scenes.title: What the week earned
scenes.speaker: sigrun
scenes.context: Each shield sells for the amount stored in price.
scenes.prompt: Write an expression for this week's revenue: the total number of shields times the price.
hints: You already have total and price. Multiply them.
scenes.explanation: Expressions combine variables with operators: total * price. If the price changes next week, the program still gives the right answer.

scenes.title: Predict the output
scenes.speaker: sigrun
scenes.context: Before running this line, predict what it prints.

options.feedback: Yes: 32 / 3 is 10.666…, and round(…, 1) keeps one decimal place, rounding up to 10.7.
Close, but round() rounds to the nearest value. 10.666… is nearer 10.7 than 10.6.
That would be round(…) with no decimal places. The 1 asks for one decimal place.
That's the average over 4 weeks. This line divides by 3.

hints: Work from the inside out: sum(orders) first, then / 3, then round.
scenes.explanation: Reading code inside-out, like Python does, lets you predict results and spot mistakes before running anything.

scenes.title: The tally runs again
scenes.speaker: sigrun
lines: It runs! Totals, averages, revenue, and not a single shout.
You didn't guess. You read what the error said and fixed exactly that.
Take this knowledge to the Great Hall one day. They love a good number up there.
